Here is how we can list the models that contain data for variables pr, tas at hourly frequency using intake-esgf in python:
```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["pr", "tas"]
frequency = ["1hr"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["gpp", "pr", "tas", "mrso"]
frequency = ["6hr"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

Right! Here is how we can name the models that have variables tos, evspsbl at day frequency using intake-esgf in python:
```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["tos", "evspsbl"]
frequency = ["day"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["gpp", "pr", "tas", "mrso"]
frequency = ["fx"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```

```python
from intake_esgf import ESGFCatalog

# initialize the catalog
cat = ESGFCatalog()

# specify variables to search for
variables = ["tos", "evspsbl"]
frequency = ["mon"]

# search the catalog for models with the specified variable
search_results = cat.search(
    variable_id=variables
    frequency=frequency
)

# get a list of unique models
models = sorted(search_results.df["source_id"].unique())

# print out our results
print(f"Models({len(models)} results):")
for i, model in enumerate(models):
    print(f"{i+1}. {model}")
```
